item.content:encoded:
PHOENIX -- Varias latas de cerveza fueron vaciadas sobre la cabeza de Aaron Judge mientras el capitán de los Yankees permanecía en el centro del clubhouse de visitantes en el Target Field la semana pasada, rodeado de compañeros eufóricos que celebraban la clasificación del club a la postemporada.
Judge entrecerró los ojos por el ardor y les advirtió a sus compañeros: “Me las van a pagar”.
Aun así, no pretenden que ésa sea su última celebración, pues tienen un firme control del primer puesto del Comodín de la Liga Americana y el título del Este de la Liga Americana todavía está en juego.
“Siempre es bueno cuando puedes celebrar esos momentos durante una temporada”, dijo el manager de los Yankees, Aaron Boone. “Mucha gente dedica mucho tiempo, esfuerzo y sudor. Obviamente, éste es apenas el primer paso de lo que esperamos sean muchos”.
Ahora que aseguraron su pase a la postemporada, ¿qué más les espera a los Yankees?
¿Cómo podría quedar el roster para la postemporada?
C: Austin Wells, Ali Sánchez 
1B: Luis García Jr., Paul Goldschmidt
2B: Jazz Chisholm Jr.
3B: Ryan McMahon, Amed Rosario
SS: George Lombard Jr., José Caballero
OF: Cody Bellinger, Trent Grisham, Spencer Jones, Heliot Ramos
BD: Ben Rice
LA: Gerrit Cole, Cam Schlittler, Max Fried
R: David Bednar, Paul Blackburn, Brent Headrick, Tim Hill, Clarke Schmidt, Michael Fulmer, John Schreiber, Will Warren, Carlos Rodón
Los Yankees utilizaron a 12 lanzadores y a 14 bateadores cuando recibieron a los Medias Rojas en la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana del año pasado, así que partiremos de esa misma premisa para el 2026.
Cole está programado para lanzar el miércoles contra Tampa Bay, mientras que Schlittler lo hará el jueves. Mirando hacia adelante, eso sugiere que Cole tendría un día adicional de descanso antes del Juego 1 de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, mientras que Schlittler estaría con su descanso normal.
Es posible que los Yankees estén alineando a Cole para abrir el Juego 1 y a Schlittler para el Juego 2. Hasta ahora, han preferido no decir mucho al respecto, salvo por la confirmación de Boone de que Cole realizará una apertura en la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana.
Rodón podría estar en el bullpen para la serie. En nuestra proyección del roster lo tenemos activo, mientras que el dominicano Luis Gil y Ryan Yarbrough figuran entre quienes quedarían fuera. Ryan Weathers trabaja para regresar como relevista, pero el tiempo juega en su contra. Si está saludable, podría ocupar el lugar de Fulmer o Schreiber.
Chisholm espera regresar esta semana para la serie contra los Rays tras sufrir un esguince en el pulgar derecho, mientras que Grisham ha mostrado mejoría y podría quedarse con un puesto en los jardines. De no ser así, Max Schuemann está entre las alternativas. Otro aspecto para seguir: ¿Podrían los Yankees incluir a Anthony Volpe en lugar de Rosario? Es una posibilidad que vale la pena considerar.
¿Cuándo comenzará la postemporada?
Si los Yankees terminan disputando la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, ésta empezará el 29 de septiembre. La Serie Divisional de la Liga Americana arrancará el 3 de octubre.
¿Contra quién jugarían los Yankees si la temporada terminara hoy?
En estos momentos, sería una revancha de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana del año pasado, con los Yankees recibiendo a los Medias Rojas en el Bronx. Los Yankees ganaron aquella serie dos victorias por una.
Este año, los Yankees tuvieron marca de 7-6 contra Boston.
¿Todavía pueden ganar el Este de la Liga Americana?
Sí, pero tienen un camino cuesta arriba. Los Yankees tienen por delante cuatro enfrentamientos directos con los Rays a partir del martes en el Yankee Stadium, incluyendo una doble-cartelera para abrir la serie. Tampa Bay domina actualmente la serie particular por 6-3, lo que significa que los Yankees necesitarían barrer para quedarse con el criterio de desempate entre ambos.
¿Quién abriría el Juego 1 por los Yankees?
Como se mencionó anteriormente, Cole está programado para lanzar el miércoles frente a Tampa Bay y Schlittler lo hará al día siguiente. Por lo tanto, Cole tendría un día adicional de descanso antes del Juego 1 de la Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana, mientras que Schlittler estaría con su descanso normal.
Después de permitir siete jonrones en sus dos aperturas anteriores, Cole mermó las dudas externas sobre una posible apertura en los playoffs con una sólida actuación en Arizona. Fried y Rodón han lidiado con lesiones, pero están recuperando su mejor nivel en el momento indicado.
Warren realizará una apertura más durante la serie contra los Orioles, según Boone, pero llegará a los playoffs como una interesante alternativa para el relevo.
¿Será Judge un factor en los playoffs?
Los Yankees han sido poco específicos sobre el estado de Judge. Boone ha evitado ofrecer un plazo estimado para su recuperación e incluso revelar el grado del tirón en la pantorrilla derecha. En términos generales, hasta un tirón de Grado 1, el de menor gravedad, requiere de dos a tres semanas para una recuperación completa.
Es casi seguro que Judge intentará regresar antes. La primera fecha en la que podría ser activado sería para el Juego 162, el 27 de septiembre. Tal como está el panorama ahora mismo, existe una posibilidad muy real de que los Yankees no cuenten con Judge al menos para una potencial Serie del Comodín de la Liga Americana.
Judge dijo que le “gustaría” estar activo para la postemporada y que ése es “el plan”, pero no dijo necesariamente que sería para el 29 de septiembre.
¿Cuáles son las otras preocupaciones en cuanto a lesiones?
Grisham ha avanzado en su programa progresivo de correr y debe de estar disponible para el roster de los playoffs, aunque Boone dijo que no será activado antes de que termine la temporada regular. Chisholm ha estado bateando y realizando tiros, y debe de ser activado durante la serie contra los Rays. Si sufre algún contratiempo, Volpe entraría en consideración.
Y aunque los Yankees no han descartado a Giancarlo Stanton, quien ha estado bateando, han ofrecido pocas novedades sobre su recuperación del más reciente tirón en la pantorrilla.

item.title: [Yanks Go Yard] Latest Clarke Schmidt injury scare yet another reminder of Yankees' insane trade deadline strategy

item.content:encoded:
More than almost any other New York Yankees playoff run, this October's edition will provide either immediate vindication for Brian Cashman's trade deadline strategy or all-new reasons to directly blame him for the team's failure. It should be fascinating to watch, if you don't actually have much emotional energy invested in the team's well-being. Clarke Schmidt's postgame note on Sunday evening was just another reason to be anxious about the way this bullpen was constructed and the amount of variables therein.
Trade deadline predictions for the Yankees' haul this year were astoundingly easy to make. A catcher, first and foremost. An impact bat, that was obvious. And then two bullpen arms to help save their late-inning core from running aground before the year ended. Maybe one would be a certified ace, a tier below Mason Miller, but still devilish. Maybe another would be a bounce back candidate or a never-was, someone who Matt Blake could unearth. Either way, the choices were many, but the outcome was obvious: CashGod would be trading for some relievers. Plural.
But then the deadline came and went. We weren't disappointed by the quality of the haul, but rather in a whole new way. No catcher? No relievers? Was this a mistake? Is the deadline tomorrow?
Nope. Cashman went all in and decided that either the prices were too high or not commensurate with the talent available. Instead, he would look the other way and ignore the rising cost of wear-and-tear in August and piece together some bullpen reinforcements using alternate levers. The waiver wire became his friend. His rotation became a plucking ground, as did his own Injured List. Will Clarke Schmidt, Ryan Weathers, Luis Gil, Will Warren, John Schreiber and Michael Fulmer be more valuable together than any names he could've added on Aug. 3? That's the bet. We'll see. I have my doubts, but he has his agenda.
And, in case you weren't already lacking confidence, Schmidt's bicep barked on Sunday and prevented him from entering the game, a game that ace reliever Brent Headrick lit on fire with an average fastball that dipped about a mile and a half below his standard velocity on the season. Hmm. If only he could've been rested during the dog days of summer.
Clarke Schmidt's worrisome postgame comments, Brent Headrick outing vs. Diamondbacks tell the same Yankees story
So, for the record, that's Schmidt - after one MLB outing this year - admitting that, out of precaution, he stopped warming up when his arm barked. His rehab was also halted along the way when he felt forearm cramping on Aug. 4, just one day post-trade deadline. The Yankees getting him back to the MLB level after a summer 2025 Tommy John surgery is remarkable. This is not someone a team should be relying on to cover meaningful postseason innings. And yet.
Headrick's stumble comes in an otherwise phenomenal year, and even as he's lost some gas down the stretch, he's still managed to mostly make things work. He's an expert at limiting inherited runners from scoring, and he's alternated spotless outings with troublesome ones post-deadline. No one knows for certain whether bringing on an experienced seventh-inning guy or two in early August would've prevented the effects of overuse from piling up on Headrick's left arm, but we do know having a viable alternative now could help them deemphasize Headrick if he's struggling to recapture his former glory. Batters hit .345 off him in 15 August games.
That group of alternatives probably doesn't, or shouldn't, include Schmidt, who's hanging on by a thread. Again, it'll be Cashman's crew - Schreiber, Fulmer, Warren, and maybe Weathers, who won't be rehabbing in a regular season game - vs. the field to see who's better equipped for October. Fascinating, if it weren't so presumptuous.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees won't win the American League East after dropping two out of three games to the Arizona Diamondbacks and are now looking at another Wild Card series against the Boston Red Sox. The rest of this season will now be about figuring out their roster heading into October, and this Rays series won't mean much.
There are plenty of questions from fans about what the roster should look like in the final week of the season. And if you're curious about that, reach out to Joseph Randazzo on X or Instagram at @YankeeLibrarian. Fans can ask anything, from questions about bullpen trust trees to what to do with Jazz Chisholm Jr. when he's activated.
The state of the bullpen
Who do you trust in the bullpen outside of Paul Blackburn, Brent Headrick, and David Bednar?@Mattmann1199 on Instagram
At this point, the two best names behind them are Will Warren and John Schreiber. It's likely that they'll be without Ryan Weathers, and that is the name I would have gone with. Now it's probably Schreiber, but I'm not too convinced about this answer.
Since Luis Gil has been blowing 100 out of the bullpen, they can see what they have in him as a pen arm heading into October. None of these answers inspire much, but they have somehow been one of the best bullpens in baseball.
A returning bat
Where should Jazz Chisholm Jr. play when they activate him@theezratakeshita on Instagram
Chisholm should probably go to second base. Volpe has been okay, but since his big debut against the Colorado Rockies, he has gone 7-for-33. He has two doubles, three stolen bases, and two RBI.
Since Boston has a ton of lefty starters, they can probably start a game with Volpe and then go to Chisholm later. That feels like what the Yankees will do, and it's probably the case if Volpe is scorching the ball. Of course, there is still time for Volpe to make things interesting here.
Judge's World Series dreams
The World Series window for Judge is closing. Might he go without ever winning one?@_not_mikeee on Instagram
That is absolutely on the table. There are some great players who have never won a championship. Dan Marino, Barry Bonds, and Henrik Lundqvist never got their ring. Granted, the Scott Hunter character in Heated Rivalry feels like it's loosely based on mid-2010s Lundqvist, but that might only half-count since it's a work of fiction.
A wild storyline would be the Yankees winning a World Series this year without Judge. Imagine the chaos of his legacy talks if that happens.
Job statuses
Is there a scenario that gets Cash or Boone fired this year?@kirby.phillips7 on Instagram
These questions are always easy to answer. Probably not this year. Cashman will probably go out on his own accord. Boone is the most likely candidate to get fired, but there aren't many teams that are going to axe a manager who kept their team afloat and in postseason contention with the amount of injuries they had. When baseball comes back after the lockout, those two will probably still be here.
Missing the playoffs again might do it for them, but the last time that happened, they stayed. It does feel like they have unlimited security in New York.
Joe Randazzo is a reference librarian who lives on Long Island. When he’s not behind a desk offering assistance to his patrons, he writes about the Yankees for Yankees On SI. Follow him as @YankeeLibrarian on X and Instagram.

item.content:encoded:
NUEVA YORK — Los Yankees se han pasado casi todo septiembre organizando a los lanzadores para la fase de octubre.
Gerrit Cole está en la lista para ser el lanzador titular en la Serie de Comodín. Cam Schlittler se ha ganado un sitio en esa misma conversación.
Max Fried vuelve a la rotación, mientras que Carlos Rodón y Will Warren están en la lista para lanzar como relevos una vez que empiece la postemporada. Estas decisiones han dejado poco margen para que algún aspirante de última hora se cuele de nuevo en el grupo de titulares.
Eso limitó las opciones de Clarke Schmidt incluso antes de que volviera a incorporarse a la plantilla. Su regreso tras una segunda operación de Tommy John nunca se planteó con el objetivo de volver a alcanzar el volumen de trabajo de un lanzador titular en las dos últimas semanas.
Los Yankees lo incorporaron al plantilla el 16 de septiembre para aportar duración, lanzamientos certeros y una variedad de lanzamientos propios de un abridor desde el bullpen. No había jugado en las Grandes Ligas desde el 3 de julio de 2025, y solo había lanzado siete entradas en las ligas menores durante su rehabilitación.
Schmidt volvió esa noche en Minnesota y consiguió dos outs, permitiendo dos sencillos de rebote y ponchando a dos. Fue su primera aparición en las Grandes Ligas en 14 meses y medio. Y lo más importante para los Yankees es que supuso el inicio de una prueba para un papel que requiere una rutina diferente.
En lugar de un día fijo de salida y una larga preparación previa al partido, Schmidt ahora tiene que entrar en calor rápidamente, salir al campo en medio de la acción o en una entrada limpia, y recuperarse siguiendo el horario de un relevista.
La situación de la plantilla ya no dejaba margen para que volviera a la rotación. Según las previsiones actuales de la MLB para la postemporada de los Yankees, Cole, Schlittler y Fried figuran como titulares, mientras que Schmidt, Rodon y Warren están entre las opciones de relevo.
Aaron Boone ha confirmado que Cole será el lanzador titular en una posible serie de comodín. Warren tiene prevista una última salida como titular en la temporada regular antes de pasar al bullpen. La posibilidad de que Schmidt volviera a ser titular se había convertido en algo más teórico que práctico para este octubre.
Un problema en el bíceps interrumpe la única prueba que le quedaba a Schmidt
Esa diferencia se hizo aún más evidente el domingo en Arizona. Clarke Schmidt estaba calentando para lo que habría sido su segunda salida desde la operación cuando notó un calambre en el bíceps derecho durante la derrota de los Yankees por 8-4 ante los Diamondbacks en el Chase Field. Dejó de lanzar y no llegó a salir al campo.
Los Yankees dijeron que las pruebas de fuerza no indicaban ningún problema en el hombro ni en el codo. Se espera que Schmidt vea a un médico del equipo en Nueva York, sin que, por el momento, se hayan previsto más pruebas.
Schmidt explicó por qué se negó a seguir adelante a pesar de esa sensación tan pronto después de la operación. Respondía a la pregunta de si ese episodio sugería un contratiempo estructural.
«No es nada estructural, fue más bien por precaución», dijo Schmidt. «Obviamente, dadas las circunstancias, al estar recuperándome de una operación, no quiero forzar nada. Todas las pruebas salieron bien, ni el hombro ni el codo presentan problemas. Era más bien una sensación parecida a un calambre. No he tenido ningún problema al atrapar la pelota hoy por la mañana y en los últimos días me he sentido muy fuerte. Así que fue algo muy, muy leve, solo por precaución».
Boone dijo que Schmidt no pudo terminar su calentamiento a pesar de haber superado las pruebas iniciales.
«Espero que no sea nada grave, pero sí lo suficiente como para que no entre en el partido», dijo Boone. «Ya veremos qué pasa».
En su lugar, Tim Hill lanzó la sexta entrada. Los Yankees habían conseguido una ventaja de 4-1 gracias a los jonrones de Heliot Ramos, George Lombard Jr. y Spencer Jones en la tercera entrada, antes de que Arizona anotara cinco carreras en la quinta, coronadas por el grand slam de Nolan Arenado ante Brent Headrick. Justin Martínez se llevó la victoria, Headrick la derrota y no se acreditó ningún salvamento.
Un historial de 67 partidos como titular se enfrenta a un futuro repleto de jugadores en los Yankees
Schmidt ya ha demostrado que puede ser titular en las Grandes Ligas. Según los registros de la MLB, 67 de sus 97 partidos como profesional han sido como titular. Tiene una efectividad de 3,82 en 393 1/3 entradas y registró una efectividad de 3,32 en 14 partidos como titular en 2025, antes de que un problema en el codo le obligara a dar por terminada la temporada.
La pregunta es si los Yankees todavía tienen un hueco real en la rotación de titulares para él. Según los registros públicos de contratos, Cole y Rodon tienen contrato hasta 2028 y Fried hasta 2032. Schlittler se ha consolidado como lanzador titular de primera línea, mientras que Warren sigue bajo el control del club. Schmidt podrá acogerse al arbitraje en 2027 y podrá convertirse en agente libre tras esa temporada.
Las reacciones en Internet pasaron rápidamente del domingo al invierno. Los aficionados se preguntaban por la resistencia de Schmidt, cómo encajaría junto a Luis Gil y si los Yankees podrán contar con él para lanzar entradas decisivas en octubre.
Ningún responsable de los Yankees ha dicho que Schmidt no vuelva a ser titular en Nueva York. Pero la profundidad de la rotación, su plazo de recuperación y los planes de los Yankees para la postemporada lo han dejado relegado a un segundo plano, con tantas opciones de titulares que ya no puede seguir siendo tu opción predeterminada.
Los Yankees necesitan que Schmidt demuestre que la transición al bullpen funciona
Por eso es tan importante lo del bíceps, aunque las noticias médicas sigan siendo positivas. Schmidt no está intentando llegar a los 90 lanzamientos. Lo que quiere es demostrar que puede calentar rápido, salir al campo cuando lo necesiten y recuperarse para otra salida.
La transición ya ha dado lugar a dos momentos incómodos. Schmidt calentó el sábado por la noche, pero Boone se decantó por Michael Fulmer en la novena entrada de un partido empatado. Fulmer encajó el jonrón de dos carreras de Pavin Smith que decidió el partido. El domingo, Schmidt estuvo a punto de salir al campo, pero unos calambres se lo impidieron.
Los Yankees tienen un balance de 89-66, a seis partidos del Tampa Bay en la División Este de la Liga Americana, cuando quedan siete partidos por disputar, según la clasificación de la MLB. Ya se han asegurado una plaza en la postemporada y ocupan el primer puesto de comodín de la Liga Americana. Su última semana empieza el martes en el Yankee Stadium contra los Rays.
Si Schmidt pasa la prueba, esos partidos supondrán un reto más sencillo. Su objetivo inmediato ya no es volver a ganarse un puesto en la rotación. Se trata de demostrar a los Yankees que pueden confiar en él en el bullpen cuando empiece octubre.
¿Qué te parece? Deja tu comentario aquí abajo.

item.content:encoded:
For a little while, it looked like it might be yet another rough outing for Gerrit Cole as the New York Yankees get closer to the playoffs.
Cole allowed a two-run home run to Arizona Diamondbacks superstar Corbin Carroll in the bottom of the second inning.
The Yankees had spotted Cole a five-run lead, but with the way the veteran right-hander has pitched lately, that didn't feel as safe as it potentially would've in the past.
On this Friday night, though, Cole was sharp from there. He didn't allow another run.
Cole eventually went 6.0 innings to earn a quality start, allowing four hits and those two runs while not walking any hitters. He struck out six while improving his season record to 9-9 and his ERA to 3.63.
Ryan Yarbrough, Michael Fulmer and Luis Gil polished the game off out of New York's bullpen in a 9-2 win that improved the Yankees to 89-64.
This night was about a lot of Yankees, including Ben Rice with a triple and a home run, and George Lombard Jr. with a home run as part of a five-run first.
But the most crucial thing that happened for New York was that Cole found his groove again. They'll need him sharp in the playoffs, and with only a couple more outings for him before then, this was a great step in the right direction.
Cole also made a fun bit of history in the process.
Gerrit Cole's New MLB History
Cole has now won the most games in an MLB career for any pitcher drafted No. 1 overall, according to MLB's Sarah Langs.
This was the 162nd pitching win of Cole's career.
The previous record was held by Mike Moore, who won 161 games after being the first overall pick in 1981.
David Price holds third place on the list with 157 wins after going in the top spot in 2007.
Cole can now expand on this record going forward, and considering how many fewer pitching wins starting pitchers are getting in this era, he probably has a chance to push the record out of reach if he has a few more solid seasons.
Gerrit Cole Draft
Cole was the No. 1 overall pick in the 2011 MLB Draft out of UCLA.
Four pitchers began the 2011 draft. The Mariners picked lefty Danny Hultzen out of Virginia second. The Diamondbacks chose Cole's UCLA teammate Trevor Bauer third. And the Orioles snagged high school righty Dylan Bundy fourth.
The first hitter chosen was high school outfielder Bubba Starling to the Royals at the fifth pick.
The National stook Rice slugger Anthony Rendon at No. 6.
The Diamondbacks were back on the board at No. 7 to get Archie Bradley, a high school righty.
The back-to-back picks at Nos. 8 and 9 were Francisco Lindor and Javier Baez to the Indians and Cubs, then the Padres got Cory Spangenberg at No. 11 before the Astros chose George Springer with the 11th pick.
It was a fascinating start to a draft, to be sure, with Cole living up to his hype.
This article was originally published on HEAVY
The post Yankees' Gerrit Cole Sets All-Time MLB Record appeared first on HEAVY.

item.content:encoded:
The two starting pitchers entered this game trending in opposite directions. Gerrit Cole had just allowed the most home runs (seven) in a two-start span in his career, while Eduardo Rodriguez is in the midst of a career year with a 2.62 ERA. One of those trends remained — Cole giving up another home run on a fastball — but fortunately the other trend was momentarily halted, the Yankees scoring five in the first off E-Rod to give themselves enough of a cushion to weather Cole’s continued home run woes.
Cole settled down after the Carroll dinger to give the Yankees six innings, by which time the offense all but put this game out of reach. They kept the pressure on, scoring a further four runs including solo home runs by Ben Rice and George Lombard Jr., to cruise to a series-opening victory in the desert, 9-2.
Rodriguez came into this game with an ERA above six in the first inning and an ERA right around two for the subsequent innings combined. That made it imperative that the Yankees find a way to do damage before the home team had a chance to come to bat, especially with the rate Cole is giving up the long ball. They did just that with a clear disciplined approach not to expand the zone against E-Rod’s curveball.
Paul Goldschmidt drew a leadoff walk, Cody Bellinger followed with a single, and Heliot Ramos also walked to load the bases with no outs. Rice drew the Yankees’ third walk in the first four batters to plate Goldschmidt and open the scoring, Goldy, Ramos, and Rice all working full counts before taking the free pass. Amed Rosario then fought off a cutter that handcuffed him up and in, muscling it to the opposite field perfectly between center and left fielder to plate Bellinger as the runners went station to station. A wild pitch allowed Ramos to score and Rice and Rosario to move up to second and third. This set up a two-run ground ball single from Lombard that just got by Geraldo Perdomo’s diving attempt to atone for his defensive misplay in the 13th that allowed the Twins to walk off the Yankees on Wednesday.
Rodriguez struck out Volpe to end the inning giving him three strikeouts in the frame, but the damage was done. The 45 pitches he threw were the most he’s thrown in the first inning in his career. 33 of those pitches fell out of the zone, but only eight induced a chase.
It’s a good thing they hung such a crooked number, because Cole immediately gave two of those runs back. He gave up a leadoff single to Perdomo before yanking an 0-1 four-seamer right into Corbin Carroll’s nitro zone, the three-time All-Star obliterating it to right for a two-run bomb to reduce the Yankees’ lead, 5-2. Rice made sure to immediately tilt the momentum back in his team’s favor. After falling behind 0-2, he stayed back on an elevated heater from E-Rod riding it out the other way and over the fence in left-center for a leadoff bomb, his 39th of the year, to give Cole some more of his cushion back, 6-2.
Cole settled down to work a scoreless third and fourth, helped in part by a sharp uptick in slider usage at the expense of some four-seamers as well as an impressive sliding catch in left-center by Spencer Jones in the third. He finally began dialing the fastball command to the corners in the fifth, striking out Tim Tawa and Lars Nootbaar on four-seamers to end the frame after Jesús Sánchez singled with one out. This allowed Lombard to restore the Yankees’ five run lead in the sixth, the rookie punishing a hanging curveball from E-Rod by lining the solo shot down the line it left and into the bullpen for his fourth of the year and third RBI on the night.
The four-seamer was the prime culprit for Cole in his previous two starts with a 68.2-percent hard-hit rate and just six whiffs, and that remained the case tonight. However, I believe it is Cole’s rustiness with his secondaries that is leading his four-seamer to get barreled. The fastball still has plenty of velocity — at 97 mph it’s a full tick above last season. I will grant that he has missed location in the zone on numerous occasions which hasn’t done him any favors.
However, after his last start, Cole identified a lack of chase and whiff against his secondaries as the reason his fastball is getting crushed. Hitters being able to lay off those chase pitches forces Cole to overuse the fastball in counts that favor the softer stuff, which in essence gives them the opportunity to hunt the heater when they should be defending against the breaker. When you can hunt a fastball in any count, chances are you are going to do damage when Cole misses his spot in the zone, the high velocity not much of a weapon when hitters’ bats are preemptively sped up.
Indeed, once he started commanding his slider and knuckle curve to the shadow of the zone in the middle innings, the hard contact against the fastball dried up. Having pitched a strong fifth and sixth and with his pitch count at 90, Boone saw no reason to overextend Cole and ended his night after six with his best innings freshest in mind. He finished night having pitched six innings, allowing two runs on four hits with no walks and six strikeouts.
Despite possessing one of the stingiest bullpens in baseball, the Diamondbacks decided that a five-run deficit in the seventh was too steep to justify using their high leverage arms. So, Zac Gallen made his first career relief appearance, the former All-Star in the midst of am injury-plagued, below-replacement-level campaign. He allowed a leadoff single to Goldschmidt and walked Ramos and Rice — again, both in full counts — to load the bases with one out. Aaron Boone sent out Ryan McMahon to pinch-hit for Rosario, and he hit a sharp grounder to first that Pavin Smith gloved but airmailed the underhand toss to Gallen covering first as all the runners were safe and a run scored on the error. Spencer Jones then appeared to ground into the inning-ending double play, but his hustle out of the box and down the line just beat the throw to pick up an RBI and make it 9-2.
Ryan Yarbrough pitched 1.1 innings in relief of Cole and worked himself into and out of trouble in the seventh. Arizona put runners on second and third as Nolan Arenado singled and Carroll doubled with one out. However, Yarbrough struck out Jose Fernandez and Tawa to strand the pair in scoring position. Rice smoked his fourth triple of the year in the ninth but was stranded at third by a McMahon strikeout. Michael Fulmer and Luis Gil recorded the final five outs of the game without allowing a baserunner to seal the win, 9-2. With the Rays having lost to the Red Sox earlier in the evening, the Yankees’ deficit is back to four games in the division, making that looming four-game set against Tampa in the Bronx even more high stakes.
Cam Schlittler looks to cement his AL Cy Young case tomorrow after Dylan Cease suffered his shortest start of the season on Friday. The Yankees ace will face off against Brandon Pfaadt with a slightly more reasonable game start time. First pitch is scheduled for 8:10 pm ET with the broadcast remaining on YES.
Yankees rout the D-Backs, 9-2, who's your Player of the Game?
Gerrit Cole pitched 6 innings of 2-run ball. George Lombard Jr. hit a two-run single and a solo homer. Ben Rice raked with a solo homer, triple, and two walks.

item.content:encoded:
It wasn't all bad news from a discouraging and frustrating 13-inning defeat at the hands of the Minnesota Twins on Wednesday afternoon, even if it really, really stung for a number of reasons.
The ray of sunshine in what was a rough day for the Yankees' divisional hopes was the return of someone they view as crucial to their chances at a deep playoff run. After a 440-day absence due to Tommy John surgery, Clarke Schmidt made his Yankees return, tossing two-thirds of an inning in the seventh before being removed due to pitch count.
It wasn't the cleanest outing, as he wasn't able to get through a full inning after throwing 24 pitches to four batters, but for someone on a big league mound for the first time in 14 months, you had to like what you saw, striking out a pair and only surrendering a pair of soft-hit singles.
The runway is rather short for the remainder of the season with just 10 games left, but Schmidt will likely see his way into four or so games down the stretch. That gives him a total of five outings to truly figure out where he can fit into a wide-open bullpen trust tree.
Clarke Schmidt's bullpen experience
Converting a full-time starter to the bullpen is not always as easy as it seems, but it's a transition the Yankees will have to make three times as we head into the postseason, with Ryan Weathers' likely return and Will Warren's place in the rotation. That said, Schmidt has a bit of an advantage.
Before becoming a full-time starter at the major-league level in 2023, Schmidt was used almost exclusively as a reliever in his brief big-league stints, most notably in 2022, when he posted a 3.12 ERA in 57.2 innings as part of a makeshift bullpen that got very good results. He didn't get himself high up the totem pole, but he pitched some important innings for the club.
His playoff experience as a reliever was unfortunately one to forget. He was saddled with a pair of losses, first in Game 3 of the ALDS after a squeaker by Oscar Gonzalez got through the infield for a walk-off single, and the second in Game 1 of the ALCS against the Houston Astros, where he allowed home runs to Yuli Gurriel and Chas McCormick in the sixth inning of what would be the start of a sweep.
He was supposed to be in the bullpen the following season, but a mountain of injuries forced him to step up in the rotation, starting what became a nightmarish 2023 season. Since then, Schmidt has made 63 appearances through his season-ending elbow surgery in 2025, all but one as a starter.
That's not in the cards for 2026, so what can he do to be useful for the Yankees in the playoffs?
Where Schmidt could fit into unstable bullpen
Schmidt adds a multi-inning righty option to a bullpen that has a lot of moving parts. He leaned hard on a cutter-slider combo on Wednesday, but also featured his sinker, four-seamer, and curveball. His velocity looked as firm as ever, something that could be enhanced but didn't need to hold back for 100 pitches.
The bullpen's premier multi-inning righty is Paul Blackburn, who relies on a ton of spin and movement in his profile, making him more volatile in games with shoddy command. He, along with closer David Bednar and lefty Brent Headrick, makes up the team's three highest-leverage arms, but it's wide open beneath them, particularly after Fernando Cruz's elbow injury.
John Schreiber has been effective as a righty specialist in a small sample, so he feels like the leader in the clubhouse as the team's sixth-inning arm, but he might not be playable in certain matchups due to his struggles against lefties. Tim Hill's overall struggles, even if he remains sharp against lefties, will also give pause. Michael Fulmer and Luis Gil haven't pitched enough to earn trust in leverage.
There are two ways that Schmidt can be deployed. One of which is as the team's right-handed bridge reliever, as sort of a "platoon" with Ryan Yarbrough (or Weathers, when he returns). Lineups with more right-handed hitters will fare significantly better against Weathers or Yarbrough if the team needs them to come into a big spot to provide some length to the back-end guys, so having a guy with the opposite hand who can fill that role is valuable.
But that role could be reserved for Warren, who's more stretched out than Schmidt and isn't at risk of being removed due to a long inning. I doubt Schmidt would be permitted to throw much more than 30 pitches in a game. That could lead the 30-year-old to be more in the Schreiber role as the sixth-inning guy, possibly pitching in higher leverage if needed due to overuse.
There are a lot of questions about Schmidt as we come down the stretch, but the important thing is that he's back and he's healthy. The more bullpen depth, the merrier.

item.content:encoded:
On Thursday night, the New York Yankees are off following a series with the Minnesota Twins at Target Field.
They won two out of three games in the series (but lost 5-4 on Wednesday).
The Yankees will now open up a series with the Arizona Diamondbacks on Friday night in Phoenix.
New York Yankees Star Luis Gil Sends Out Post
Ahead of their series in Arizona, Luis Gil made a post to Instagram.
He wrote: “🤷🏻♂️”
Looking At Gil
Gil is in the middle of his 5th season at the MLB level (all with the Yankees).
He got off to a strong start to his career (and was the American League Rookie of The Year).
In 2024, Gil went 15-7 with a 3.50 ERA in 29 starts.
Gil struggled at the start of this season (and was sent to Triple-A).
Since he’s been back with the Yankees, the 28-year-old has been a reliever.
This year, Gil has gone 1-2 with a 5.40 ERA in six games (four starts).
Looking At The Yankees Ahead Of Arizona
The Yankees are the second-place team in the American League East with an 88-64 record in 152 games.
They have won seven out of their last ten games (and are 46-32 in 78 games on the road).
Following their series in Arizona, the Yankees will return home to host the Tampa Bay Rays on Tuesday in the Bronx.
Looking At D-Backs Ahead Of Yankees Visit
The Diamondbacks are the third-place team in the National League West with an 80-73 record in 153 games.
They are 43-35 in 78 games at home.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are headed to the MLB playoffs! But they have a lot to figure out before they *likely* have to face the Boston Red Sox in a 3-game Wild Card series.
A big storyline surrounding the Yankees right now is what manager Aaron Boone will do with Anthony Volpe when Jazz Chisholm Jr. returns.
Since Jazz went to the IL (and Volpe was called up). Volpe has had his fair share of moments, and it begs the question: What will the Yankees' infield layout look like?
Yankees fans may hate to admit it, but with Volpe's previous playoff experience, it might be wise to give the kid a shot in October.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Predicted to 'Dump' Luis Gil Ahead of Playoffs
What Should the Yankees Do with Anthony Volpe?
Has Anthony Volpe done enough to remain on the Yankees roster? Should be play second or third base in the MLB playoffs in place of Jazz Chisholm Jr. or Ryan McMahon.
Over his last seven games, Anthony Volpe has a home run, two doubles, eight hits, 7 RBI, and scored three runs.
In all likelihood, Jazz still has his 2B spot when he returns, but Ryan McMahon?? That's another question.
Ryan McMahon’s career numbers with the Yankees:
🤮 171 G🤮 .212 AVG🤮 14 HR🤮 52 RBI🤮 .636 OPS
How would you grade McMahon’s time in pinstripes so far? pic.twitter.com/cVEPiw5FFF
— SleeperYankees (@SleeperYankees) September 17, 2026
What will Volpe's role be when Jazz comes back?
Second baseman Anthony Volpe (7 games).348 BA // 1 HR // 7 RBI // .400 OBP // .965 OPS#Yankees pic.twitter.com/cqwisk1tw7
— Fireside Yankees (@FiresideYankees) September 17, 2026
Ryan McMahon is batting .210 this season with 10 home runs, 34 RBI, and just 66 hits.
And half of his games are in a hitters' haven for lefties.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Get Strong Jasson Dominguez Message Ahead of MLB Playoffs
Anthony Volpe's 2026 Season at a Glance
While Anthony Volpe's 2026 stats don't light the world on fire, it's fair to note he hasn't been given an extended runway to make a major impact, as he's bounced between AAA and the Bigs frequently.
Across 63 games this season, Volpe is batting .253 (career-high) with 14 XBH, 26 RBI, and an OPS+ of 92 (also would be career-high).
He's cut down on some of the strikeouts, and is still working a decent amount of walks.
Yankees fans, let me know in the comments what you think Anthony Volpe's role should be with the team in October?
If it were me (and being clear, I'm not the GM!) I'd run Volpe out there in October at 3B. It gives the lineup right-left balance, and Anthony Volpe has at least shown a capability of putting the ball in play that Ryan McMahon hasn't.

The New York Yankees are officially IN the MLB playoff picture, as they recently clinched a postseason berth.
While the Yankees still have a small percentage chance to win the AL East, they will likely be in the AL Wild Card round, playing the Boston Red Sox.
In such a big series, decisions will have to be made regarding who gets a 26-man roster spot.
One player who is on the outside looking in and will likely be left off is Luis Gil.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Get Strong Jasson Dominguez Message Ahead of MLB Playoffs
Yankees Urged to Leave Luis Gil Off Playoff Roster
Recently, FanSided.com writer Jake Elman predicted a handful of players who will be 'dumped' from the playoff roster, or essentially dumped from the 26-man fold.
"But for now, Gil is on the roster bubble, and we don't expect him to crack the 26-man playoff squad. Clarke Schmidt's return gives the Yankees another depth arm, and Gil hasn't shown that he's worth carrying on a limited staff. That said, we imagine he'd be among the first names called if injuries strike his teammates. "
Gil has pitched just 23.1 innings for the Yankees this season, and carries a 5.40 ERA in that span.
So, yeah, it's fair to assume his spot on the playoff roster may not be safe.
More MLB on Heavy: New York Yankees Urged to Make Bold Paul Goldschmidt Decision
What Has Luis Gil Done in His MLB Career
Luis Gil has technically pitched in five seasons with the New York Yankees.
He briefly pitched in 2021 and 2022 with the club, but did not pitch at all in MLB in 2023 before bursting onto the scene in 2024 (AL Rookie of the Year).
However, since earning that top accolade, he has not been consistent as a member in the Yankees rotation.
Across 265.1 total IP in his career, Gil holds a very respectable 3.66 ERA, but perhaps his absence from the Bigs is a product of the Yankees' loaded rotation, rather than his individual ability.

item.content:encoded:
For their sake, the New York Yankees better hope that superstar outfielder Aaron Judge’s newest injury is only a minor setback.
Judge left Wednesday’s extra-inning loss to the Twins with lower leg tightness, immediately raising concerns among fans that he’ll miss the Yankees’ first playoff series. New York entered play on Sept. 17 in firm control of the AL’s top Wild Card seed, putting them on track to host the No. 5 Red Sox in the first round.
If Judge can’t go when the playoffs begin on Sept. 29, then he won’t be the only notable contributor not in uniform during the Wild Card Series. Each team gets 26 players for their playoff rosters, but no more than 13 pitchers. Some clubs opt for 14 position players and 12 pitchers, though we personally prefer a 13-and-13 balance. Additionally, teams can adjust their rosters between series, and obviously they can replace an injured player if needed.
For this list, we’re only including players who are healthy and active as of Sept. 17. In other words, that means Trent Grisham, Giancarlo Stanton, and Ryan Weathers are among those who didn’t qualify. We’ve also omitted Judge because the Yankees haven’t announced the severity of his left leg injury.
Jasson Domínguez, OF
The writing has long been on the wall for Domínguez, who was recently demoted to Triple-A amid another disappointing season. Even if Judge potentially misses the Wild Card Round, it’s difficult to envision the 23-year-old Domínguez returning as a backup outfielder.
Frankly, the entire situation is unfortunate, because neither Domínguez’s talent nor his work ethic has been the issue. He’s always earned rave reviews for his maturity and overall attitude, but injuries — most notably to his elbow and shoulder — have seemingly sapped him of his once-potent power stroke.
Luis Gil, P
Gil has had an odd career, winning AL Rookie of the Year in 2024 despite debuting three years earlier. Injuries have limited him to a 3.92 ERA over 80.1 innings since the start of 2025, and he recently moved to the bullpen. We’ll see whether the Yankees view the 28-year-old as a long-term reliever, or if they’d bring him to spring training as a starter.
But for now, Gil is on the roster bubble, and we don’t expect him to crack the 26-man playoff squad. Clarke Schmidt’s return gives the Yankees another depth arm, and Gil hasn’t shown that he’s worth carrying on a limited staff. That said, we imagine he’d be among the first names called if injuries strike his teammates.
Paul Goldschmidt, 1B/DH
Goldschmidt turned 39 last week, and it’s unclear whether he’s in the final weeks of a likely Hall of Fame career. He’s totaled 65.3 bWAR, and the majority of the 142 players above him are already in the Hall of Fame or will be when they’re eligible.
Let’s get back to the present. Goldschmidt is hitting just .239 with a .680 OPS in 103 second-half plate appearances, and he’s only capable of playing first or DHing. Ben Rice fills both roles, and Cody Bellinger can also play first if needed.
The one thing potentially working in Goldschmidt’s favor is his .313 average and 1.006 OPS against lefties, but that’s not enough to warrant a roster spot in our eyes. Sorry, Goldy. At least you’d finally earn a World Series ring if the Yankees finish the job.
Will Warren, SP
This might come as a surprise, given that we included Warren in our most recent playoff roster projection. But the more that we think about things, Schmidt’s return feels like a significant blow to Warren’s chances of pitching in October. Do the Yankees really need two long relievers capable of eating up innings if the starter leaves early?
We initially had veteran swingman Ryan Yarbrough in this spot, though he might have the advantage as a left-handed reliever.. He also has a 2.91 ERA in 21.2 second-half innings and has since recovered from a lingering right oblique problem.

item.content:encoded:
The New York Yankees are now in wait-and-see mode.
Aaron Judge left Wednesday’s game early with right leg tightness. There’s no word yet on whether he’ll have to miss time, and we likely won’t have an answer until Friday at the earliest.
Before then, let’s answer some of your Yankees questions in part one of our mailbag. If you want to ask anything else, there’s still time to do so here.
Note: Questions have been edited for clarity and brevity.
Advertisement
Assuming Trent Grisham is healthy, who starts in center field during the playoffs: him or Spencer Jones? — Ed H.
Yankees manager Aaron Boone told reporters Wednesday that Grisham is running “up to a decent speed” in his comeback from a right hamstring strain. Considering Grisham at normal speed is slow, it’s anyone’s guess what that actually means.
If Grisham is ready to go, it will be interesting to see what Boone decides. There are numerous examples of the Yankees opting for the veteran over an inexperienced player like Jones when the games matter most.
Both players have their warts. Neither Grisham nor Jones is a good defensive center fielder. Jones looked abysmal in center, letting a ground ball go under his glove, dropping a fly ball that hit his glove and nearly trucking Heliot Ramos in right field. Meanwhile, Grisham has trouble getting to balls over his head and in the gaps because he’s slow-footed. There’s likely a higher floor of success, though, for Grisham. Even on the balls Jones has caught, there have been instances where he doesn’t look comfortable reading the play off the bat.
So the main difference will come down to offense.
Before Grisham injured his hamstring, he was not hitting. Calls for Jones to take over were already happening. To Jones’ credit, he has produced at the plate. Even after a dreadful 0-for-6 performance with five strikeouts on Wednesday, Jones has a 113 wRC+. He is always a threat to pop a home run, and that wins ballgames in October.
Grisham has one of the best eyes on the team, rarely strikes out and works at-bats. That matters when the batters behind him would likely be Ben Rice and Judge (depending on his health).
Not that my opinion holds any weight, but I’d stick with Jones in center field. The Yankees can always use Grisham, who’s one of the most clutch hitters on the team, in big spots off the bench.
Advertisement
What will/should the Yankees playoff rotation and bullpen look like? I hate to say it, but Gerrit Cole and Max Fried are not looking like aces these days. The team is winning Will Warren’s and Carlos Rodón’s starts. How are these facts likely to influence Boone’s postseason rotation decisions? … As soon as I say this, Fried pitches a gem. Jinx. — Aaron D.
The American League East race isn’t over yet, but the likeliest outcome is the Yankees will play in a wild-card series against the Boston Red Sox. That means the Yankees will only need three starting pitchers for the first round.
Cam Schlittler should start Game 1. There’s no argument otherwise. Schlittler is one of the very best starting pitchers in the sport. You want your best pitcher going in Game 1 to give yourself the best possible chance of not facing a must-win Game 2.
From there, it’ll be a toss-up between Fried and Cole. Both pitchers have concerns attached to them.
Fried has battled command issues all season, while Cole has allowed plenty of hard contact while not getting much swing-and-miss. I’d lean toward Fried over Cole.
As for the bullpen, the Yankees could have Rodón in case the club needs length. The others likely to be on the roster are Will Warren, David Bednar, Brent Headrick, Paul Blackburn, John Schreiber, Clarke Schmidt, Ryan Yarbrough and Ryan Weathers, if he’s healthy. I’d leave off Tim Hill, who has struggled mightily this season, Luis Gil and Michael Fulmer.
What is the realistic outlook for second base next year? Jazz Chisholm Jr. hasn’t played up to his talent, which might make him more enticing by bringing down his cost. The infield is already crowded, though, with Ryan McMahon under contract, George Lombard Jr.’s promotion, José Caballero, two first basemen (three if Paul Goldschmidt is still seen as Giancarlo Stanton insurance), and Anthony Volpe’s re-ascension. — Marco F.
What the Yankees decide to do at second base is one of the most fascinating storylines of the offseason.
Advertisement
I agree with you, Marco, that this season has likely cost Chisholm millions. He is nearing the end of his worst offensive season since 2021. He won’t reach the heights he set for himself entering 2026, but he still could reach a 20-40 season. Few players have the talent to post those numbers. Before this year, Chisholm posted back-to-back 4+ fWAR seasons. It would not be wrong for the Yankees or another team to bet on his upside.
Chisholm still offers tremendous defense at second and excellent baserunning. If his bat gets back to being considerably above average, he profiles as one of the best second basemen in the sport. There are valid concerns about his offense, though. His hit tool is considerably below average, and as he ages and loses athleticism, that could be a major problem that he cannot overcome.
The Yankees should consider giving Chisholm a short-term deal, though. He is a better option than Caballero and Volpe, who are better as role players, and few available players are better than what he can provide.
The Yankees should strongly consider playing Caballero or Volpe, who played a few games in the minors there, at third base. McMahon is one of the worst everyday regulars in the big leagues this season, and there’s a higher likelihood of Caballero or Volpe producing at the plate.
Has the Martian played his last game in a Yankees uniform? — oconnell13
It’s a hard question to answer because you can’t predict injuries. You never know if the Yankees will have to reach into the minor leagues for depth.
But it’s not far-fetched to think Jasson Domínguez will never play in another important game for the Yankees again. He cannot be trusted in the field. Every game matters for the Yankees, and there’s always a queasy feeling when the ball is hit his way.
His bat also hasn’t progressed enough to keep giving him chances to prove himself. Jones has leapfrogged him on the depth chart, and the Yankees now have Heliot Ramos on their roster. There may not be space for Domínguez.
Advertisement
What are the Yankees’ pitching plans for the rest of the regular season? Specifically, who’s lining up for the Rays series and will any of them be limited in terms of pitch count? — Nick B.
As of now, the Yankees are lined up to start their best four starters against the Rays next week. Here’s how it looks:
Tuesday: Fried and Rodón are in line to start the games of the doubleheader.
Wednesday: Cole
Thursday: Schlittler
The Rays are also on track to start their best pitchers for that series. They could start Nick Martinez and Drew Rasmussen on Tuesday, Freddy Peralta on Wednesday and Ian Seymour on Thursday. Their rotation is dependent on what they decide to do for their weekend series against the Boston Red Sox. But if they wanted, all of these pitchers could factor into their pitching plans next week.
Any chance the Yanks consider Ben Rice as the backup catcher on the postseason roster to free up an extra bench spot for someone more versatile (and better than) Ali Sánchez/J.C. Escarra? — Matthew L.
The odds of this happening are close to zero.
Earlier in the season, Rice kept catching behind the scenes. Before games, he’d catch bullpens and do on-field drills with director of catching Tanner Swanson. Rice hasn’t done any of that in months.
If anything, Rice would only be used in an emergency situation. Believe it or not, the organization believes in Sánchez. That’s why they didn’t promote Mitch Garver. Sánchez is out of minor league options, so they’d have to designate him for assignment and risk him getting claimed off waivers.
